msc1_behavior.second_zip_write: overwrites the first backup's ZIP and sidecar in place

notes: This is a D-006-style correction, not oracle parity. Source's filename timestamp (`DateFormatter` with format "yyyyMMdd-HHmmss", line 228-231) has one-second resolution, and `createBackup`'s destination path is opened for writing unconditionally -- two backups triggered in the same wall-clock second (a manual backup racing a mandatory pre-mutation/pre-restore/pre-replace safety backup that shares the same creation token, or two automatic ticks) silently overwrite each other, destroying a still-wanted recovery point with no error surfaced anywhere. Phase 6's `msc_application::backups::unique_zip_path` checks the destination before every backup is written and appends `-2`, `-3`, ... only when the plain timestamped name is already taken, preserving the readable name for the common (non-colliding) case. A disambiguated filename falls back to raw-filename display in `make_display_name` -- see `fixtures/backups/display-name-unparseable-suffix-falls-back-to-raw-filename.json`, an existing documented case, not a new one.
